picks.title: GloWild
picks.whyLine: A mile-long after-dark path of lighted treasure-hunt sculptures at the zoo, where the lantern walk itself is the draw.

picks.title: Evergy Festival of Lights
picks.whyLine: A holiday lights walk through the botanical garden that comes back every winter and anchors the season for many families.

picks.title: Tonksgiving 15
picks.whyLine: An Ozarks band's Thanksgiving-week show, now in its fifteenth edition, which gives its following a fixed date each year.

picks.title: Mayor's Christmas Tree Lighting Event
picks.whyLine: The Mayor's Christmas Tree lighting at Crown Center Square opens the city's holiday season with a youth chorus, remarks and a fireworks finale.

picks.title: Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey
picks.whyLine: The circus name nearly everyone knows, with more than a century of touring big-top shows behind it, here for a single arena weekend.

picks.title: City Market’s 9th Annual Merry Market!
picks.whyLine: A downtown open-air holiday market in its ninth year, with over 100 local makers each season.

picks.title: The Nutcracker
picks.venue: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
picks.whyLine: The city's holiday ballet at the Kauffman Center, a December staple built on Victorian-era sets and costumes that many families plan the season around.

picks.title: Phantom of the Opera
picks.whyLine: The touring staging of one of the longest-running and best-known Broadway musicals, its one stop at Music Hall in Kansas City.

picks.title: Six Math Essentials
picks.whyLine: A Fields Medalist, among the most celebrated living mathematicians, speaking for an evening in Kansas City, an appearance that seldom comes here.

picks.title: Wintersong
picks.whyLine: The Kansas City Chorale's seasonal concert in the Nelson-Atkins' Rozzelle Court, which the description calls a holiday tradition.

picks.title: Handel’s Messiah
picks.venue: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
picks.whyLine: The Kansas City Symphony's yearly performance of Handel's oratorio, a holiday-season fixture for the city's concert audience.

picks.title: Los Lobos
picks.whyLine: A band known far beyond roots music for its 1980s chart-topping hit, playing a small East Bottoms club.

picks.title: Kansas vs Missouri Men’s Basketball
picks.whyLine: Kansas and Missouri renew their basketball rivalry on neutral ground downtown, a game much of the region stops for.

picks.title: Amy Grant, Michael W. Smith, CeCe Winans
picks.whyLine: Three of the best-known names in Christian and gospel music, with decades of crossover hits, together on one Christmas bill in an arena.

picks.title: Mannheim Steamroller Christmas
picks.venue: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
picks.whyLine: A Christmas-album franchise whose synthesized carols are heard in homes far beyond any concert audience.

picks.title: Trans-Siberian Orchestra
picks.whyLine: A holiday rock-opera act known well outside rock circles, filling arenas with lasers and pyrotechnics every winter.

picks.title: The Bodyguard
picks.venue: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
picks.whyLine: A touring production of the stage musical built on the Whitney Houston film and songs, with its one Kansas City stop at the Kauffman Center.

picks.title: An Evening With Kenny G
picks.whyLine: A saxophonist whose melodic instrumental records sold in the tens of millions, known to people who own no jazz.

picks.title: Mucha’s Muses: Sarah Bernhardt and the Spirit of Art Nouveau
picks.whyLine: A major Art Nouveau exhibition on Alphonse Mucha's work for Sarah Bernhardt, the kind of show the Nelson-Atkins plans its season around.
